content: 1. The interaction between temocillin and rose hips may result in increased levels of one due to decreased renal clearance. This interaction is of minor or unknown significance, so close monitoring is recommended. 2. Rose hips can decrease the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is considered serious and applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Alternative treatments should be considered. 3. Tetracycline may decrease the levels of rose hips by increasing their elimination. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance, but close monitoring is advised. 4. Rose hips may reduce the levels of thyroid desiccated by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Rose hips can increase the levels or effects of tolfenamic acid through competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 6. Rose hips may increase the levels or effects of tolmetin by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 7. The interaction between trientine and rose hips may result in decreased levels of one due to inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended, and administration should be separated by 2 hours. 8. Rose hips may increase the levels or effects of valganciclovir through competition for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 9. Vitamin E may decrease the levels of rose hips by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is of minor or unknown significance. Close monitoring is advised. 10. Rose hips may reduce the effects of wheat germ extract through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, and the manufacturer advises separating administration by 2 hours. 11. Rose hips may increase the levels or effects of willow bark by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. Conversely, willow bark may decrease the levels of rose hips by increasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. 12. Rose hips may increase the levels of willow bark by decreasing its renal clearance. This interaction is minor and of unknown significance. Potential adverse effects of rose hips include: Kidney stones Sickle cell anemia Headache Heartburn Insomnia Nausea Pregnancy and lactation considerations: Pregnancy category: Unknown. Lactation: Considered safe. Category A: Generally acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
